ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and PCMLTFA Regulations, RR/2002-277, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46 (money-laundering offences); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, and United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2 (economic sanctions); Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), including unlimited liability corporation provisions (ss 15-16), corporate naming (s 10), director residency screening (s 102(2)), and registered office (ss 17-18); Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2022, SA 2022, c 21 (beneficial ownership register, 25% threshold); Safe Food for Canadians Act, SC 2012, c 24, and Safe Food for Canadians Regulations, SOR/2018-108; Meat Import Act, RSC 1985, c M-3, and Meat Import Regulations, SOR/89-238 (beef tariff-rate-quota import permits administered by Global Affairs Canada, Export and Import Controls Bureau).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized biometric page of each initial director's and 25%+ controlling shareholder's passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (source-country designated competent authority; Canada acceded to the Apostille Convention effective 11 January 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (bank statement or utility bill issued within 6 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original issuing bank or utility provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, followed by Hague Apostille where the holder resides outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status for any foreign corporate shareholder of the ULC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registrar (e.g., Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (source-country competent authority)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / register of directors of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate secretary or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille when executed abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to Act as First Director (statutory form), notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Canada, or notarization plus Hague Apostille for foreign-resident directors

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and senior officers against: (1) foreign and domestic PEPs and heads of international organizations as defined under PCMLTFA and RR/2002-277; (2) Global Affairs Canada consolidated SEMA and United Nations Act sanctions schedules; (3) UN Security Council Consolidated List; and (4) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists (secondary compliance touchpoint for USD SWIFT/TT and revolving LC rails). Enhanced due diligence is triggered where any 25%+ UBO is a PEP or holds a material connection to a sanctioned jurisdiction; re-screening must occur every 90 days and upon any material beneficial-ownership change; records are retained for 5 years post-relationship under PCMLTFA record-keeping requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES - Corporate Access system) via corporeregistry.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: ABCA naming rules permit only Latin-script (Roman alphabet) characters; non-Latin-script names (Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic) must be transliterated into ASCII Roman characters for the jurisdictional legal name. The legal name must conclude with the mandatory ULC designator 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or the abbreviation 'ULC' (French-form 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' permissible). Numerals and standard punctuation (commas, periods, ampersands, apostrophes) are accepted; a distinctive element plus a descriptive element are required to distinguish the name from existing CORES records.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: bank, banker, banking, trust, trustee, trust company, loan corporation, insurance, assurance - require prior financial regulator consent (Alberta Treasury Board / FSRA)
lawyer, barrister, solicitor, attorney, paralegal, legal clinic - restricted under the Legal Profession Act, RSA 2000, c L-8
accountant, accounting, auditor, audit - require CPA regulator consent
engineer, professional engineer, engineering - require APEGA consent (Engineering and Geoscience Professions Act)
university, college, institute, academy - require ministerial or post-secondary authority consent
physician, surgeon, medical, dental, pharmacy - restricted under provincial health-licensing statutes
royal, Crown, ministry, parliament, government, federal, provincial, municipal - require Crown or Ministerial consent
charitable, foundation - restricted under the Charitable Fundraising Act unless licensed
words that are obscene, scandalous, confusingly similar to an existing NUANS record, or that misstate the jurisdiction or nature of the business
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On CORES refusal, the applicant receives a written rejection notice. Counsel may: (1) file an administrative representation to the Registrar of Corporations / Director, Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) invoking the ABCA name-review discretion and requesting Ministerial consent for flagged sensitive tokens; (2) resubmit a fresh NUANS search with a materially distinct distinctive element; or (3) after final refusal, apply for judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. The administrative appeal must be initiated within 30 days of the written refusal, and any re-reservation must complete before the expiry of the original 90-day reservation window to preserve priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. ABCA requires the Articles of Incorporation to state a registered office address within Alberta that is a physical street address (not a P.O. Box); a commercial virtual-office / registered-agent service providing a physical Calgary or Edmonton address, mail forwarding and document acceptance satisfies the statutory test. For the cold-chain import business, the SFCR import licence requires an importer address in Canada where CFIA may review and access records; a virtual head office is accepted by CFIA, although the operational cold-storage import premises or customs broker's bonded facility must be separately documented for CBSA port-of-entry purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - 5-10% annualized probability of a CFIA SFCR importer verification for a licensed SME importer, and under 1% probability of an unannounced physical inspection of the virtual registered office; CBSA performs per-shipment documentary inspection of frozen meat and seafood entries at the port of entry, but this does not extend to the corporate registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Included in the NUANS search fee; no separate statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of Incorporation - Alberta ULC (online filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: CAD 250 for online filings
Provincial UBO registry fee; estimated CAD 75 within the unified corporate filing tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 — ss. 10 (incorporation), 12 (articles), 15.1–15.3 (unlimited liability corporation), 24–25 (registered office), 101–105 (directors), 140 (share consideration); Business Corporations Regulation, Alta Reg 119/2000; ULC designation is declared in the articles and recorded in the corporate register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Ministry of Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction), CorpReg online filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Form 1) filed together with Notice of Registered Office, Notice of Directors, and Consents to Act as Director, each executed by the incorporator and first directors; ULC status is declared in the articles under s. 15.1(2) ABCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for an Alberta ULC; the ABCA permits nominal subscription, e.g., 1,000 common shares subscribed at C$1.00 per share. Directors fix fair consideration for each treasury share issue under s. 140; the share register and subscription receipts evidence capitalization for bank, customs and letter-of-credit facilities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and ULC Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through a licensed Corporation Service Provider or a CorpReg-authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) request containing the proposed distinctive name and the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Review the name search report for conflicts, obtain any required third-party consent if the name contains a personal or trademarked element, and reserve the approved name for 90 days to ensure availability at incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and alternate names
Consent letters for restricted words or names of individuals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged as confusingly similar, refile a fresh NUANS report with a revised distinctive element within the 90-day reservation window; no appeal fee is charged for correction of obvious administrative errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles of Incorporation and Supporting Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and founding counsel; documents are prepared for filing with the Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) containing the corporate name, unlimited liability corporation statement, authorized share structure (1,000 common shares without par value), restriction provisions (if any), and the Alberta registered office and first directors schedule. Complete the Notice of Registered Office, Notice of Directors, and Consents to Act as Director. All first directors must sign consents; notarization is not required in Alberta.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) with ULC designation
Consents to Act as Director for each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the registry identifies missing director consents or an invalid share structure, the filing is returned with a deficiency notice; the applicant resubmits corrected documents through the same CorpReg channel before the 90-day name reservation expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-Filing of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (CorpReg online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation package to CorpReg, pay the CAD $200 incorporation fee by approved credit card or payment account, and receive the electronic Certificate of Incorporation with the unique Alberta corporate number. Verify that the certificate expressly records the unlimited liability corporation status and that the registered office and first directors are correctly reflected in the registry profile.
required_dossiers: Electronically executed Articles of Incorporation package
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a requisition before certificate issuance, respond within 30 days with amended articles; if the certificate is issued with an error, apply for rectification under s. 21(1) ABCA within the applicable statutory limitation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Secretarial Set-Up, First Board Resolutions and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the ULC; corporate records maintained at the registered office in Calgary, Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the First Board Resolution adopting the corporate seal, fixing the registered office, appointing officers, and accepting the incorporator's subscription. Adopt the general operating bylaw. Issue the share certificate for 1,000 common shares. Open the corporate minute book and registers of directors, officers, shareholders, and registered office. Maintain all statutory records for regulatory inspection.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution approved by directors
Register of directors and officers with Alberta residential addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any corporate record is missing or defective, the board may pass a ratifying resolution confirming original intent with retroactive effect, and the registers may be completed and re-paginated before the next corporate registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Import/Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated ULC for a 9-digit Business Number using the Alberta corporate number and certificate data. Simultaneously activate the GST/HST account (5% GST in Alberta) under the Excise Tax Act, the Import/Export (RM) account required for CBSA customs clearance of frozen beef and seafood, and the payroll (RP) account if employees are engaged. Appoint a licensed customs broker through the RM account to lodge import declarations under the Customs Act.
required_dossiers: Alberta corporate number and registered office details
Customs broker appointment letter for the RM account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the registration due to a corporate data mismatch, correct the registry profile in CorpReg and resubmit through BRO; an RM account denial is cured by amending the authorized importer declaration and re-attaching the customs broker mandate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Safety Codes Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Business and Safety Codes Services, together with the accredited Safety Codes Authority under Alberta's Safety Codes Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business licence for wholesale food importation and distribution of frozen meat and seafood. Submit the cold-chain warehouse lease, floor plan, and refrigeration mechanical specifications. Request fire and structural inspections under the Alberta Fire Code and building codes. Obtain the Certificate of Occupancy and OHS compliance statement before storing product or receiving inbound containers.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership certificate and premises floor plan
Building occupancy certificate and structural clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused, correct the stated bylaw or Safety Codes deficiencies, obtain revised inspection certificates, and request a hearing before the Safety Codes Appeal Board within 14 days of the refusal decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA), Safe Food for Canadians Program, in coordination with Alberta Health Services and the municipal Safety Codes Authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act Licence (Import Subclass) under the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations, SOR/2018-108, for the importation of deep-frozen beef carcasses and pelagic fish products

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), Environmental Assessment and Approvals Branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Conditional Exemption — a cold-chain wholesale warehouse is not a designated mandatory EIA activity under the Activities Designation Regulation (Alta Reg 276/2003); however, installation of ammonia refrigeration systems above the regulatory threshold or standby diesel generators triggers a targeted EPEA Registration or Approval filing before commissioning.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Municipal sewer discharge limits (e.g., City of Calgary Wastewater Bylaw 39M2006): BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 300 mg/L, fats/oils/grease ≤ 100 mg/L, pH 6.0–11.0; ammonia refrigeration systems designed to CSA B52 with immediate release reporting to AEPA under EPEA; refrigerant management per CEPA 1999 Ozone-Depleting Substances and Halocarbons Regulations; no untreated condensate or stormwater discharge to groundwater; frozen meat and seafood waste and contaminated packaging disposed under Alberta waste regulations with waste manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificate of Occupancy and fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code (Safety Codes Act, RSA 2000, c S-1); structural load inspection by an accredited Safety Codes officer for cold-storage racking and mezzanine floors; workplace clearance under the Alberta OHS Act and OHS Code covering cold-room entry procedures, ammonia detection and alarms, PPE, WHMIS training, emergency lighting and evacuation plans; municipal business licence evidencing compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; online portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/my-business-account.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC), after Alberta incorporation is complete, the company must register for a federal Business Number (BN) with the CRA. This is achieved by submitting Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or by applying online through CRA's Register online for a business number service. The BN becomes the base for a separate GST/HST account (RT program), which the importer must open for GST/HST reporting. Non-resident entities without Canadian incorporation can use a representative and file Form RC1 with supporting foreign registration documents; the CRA will assign a BN and GST/HST account number, subject to proof of foreign business identity and, where applicable, a Canadian representative agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a 'check-the-box' election analogous to the United States. For federal income tax, an Alberta ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax under the Income Tax Act. The ULC may be treated as fiscally transparent for certain foreign tax purposes (e.g., under the Canada-US tax treaty for US federal tax), but such foreign classification does not alter Canadian domestic taxation. No hybrid mismatch or partnership elections are available to convert the ULC's Canadian tax character; Canadian tax law applies the same entity-level treatment irrespective of the unlimited liability attribute.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Alberta does not impose a provincial sales tax or HST, resulting in a single federal levy.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) made in Canada; however, any person importing goods into Canada for commercial purposes may be required to register to account for GST on imported goods even if below the threshold, and voluntary registration is advisable to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently operate a national real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based clearance system for GST/HST invoices. Registered businesses must issue invoices containing prescribed information under section 223 of the Excise Tax Act. Registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1 million are required to file GST/HST returns electronically using GST/HST NETFILE, EDI, or an XML production system through CRA approved software. Standard reciprocal exchange of commercial e-invoices is permitted but not mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating on exports is available when the supplier transfers ownership of goods and delivers them to a foreign address, or delivers them to a common carrier or exporter for immediate export; the supply must be substantiated as an export under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act. Services supplied to non-residents are generally zero-rated when the service is not rendered in connection with real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada. For an importer re-exporting frozen beef or seafood, the initial import will be taxable under GST Division III, and the subsequent export supply can be zero-rated upon provision of adequate export documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A / Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED) electronic declaration)
Bill of Lading or airway bill evidencing physical export and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank transfer evidence showing receipt of foreign currency proceeds
Commercial invoice, packing list, and marine insurance certificate
Transaction and payment records (SWIFT MT103 or letter of credit drawdown documentation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years, or seven years in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. False zero-rating claims are subject to penalties under subsection 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act, gross negligence penalties equal to 50% of the net tax, and mandatory interest. Fraudulently claimed refunds can be wholly clawed back, together with monetary penalties and potential prosecution in tax court or under the Criminal Code. Businesses must preserve export evidence for six years and maintain a complete audit trail of both the import GST payment and the subsequent export sale to sustain the zero-rated treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating jointly with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank regulation, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for anti-money-laundering surveillance, and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) for Investment Canada Act administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully floating exchange-rate regime with unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility, consistent with IMF Article VIII obligations. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely deliverable both onshore and offshore; there is no exchange-licensing authority, quota system, or central-bank approval for capital movements. Profit remittance from an Alberta ULC to non-resident shareholders is subject only to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory rate, reducible under an applicable income tax treaty), with no convertibility or repatriation permit required. Material compliance hurdles are limited to (i) the Investment Canada Act notification and national-security review for establishment of a new Canadian business by a non-Canadian, (ii) FINTRAC reporting of electronic funds transfers of C$10,000 or more and enhanced beneficial-ownership disclosure, and (iii) anti-hybrid-mismatch and GAAR exposure if the ULC's pass-through election is used to create a deductible/disregarded mismatch in cross-border structures
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada abolished statutory exchange controls in 1951 and the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) imposes no obligation to surrender, convert, or repatriate export or trading proceeds. A Canadian entity may hold, spend, or lend received foreign currency without restriction. The only operational duties are statistical: Statistics Canada's International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) collects balance-of-payments data on direct-investment and trade transactions, and FINTRAC requires an electronic funds transfer report for every wire of C$10,000 or more within a 24-hour window

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Trade Finance Account with Revolving Import LC Facility and Escrow Subledger
Treasury Management Account + Cold-Chain Payables Clearing Sub-account
Operational Account with Commercial Card and FX Forward Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for use as a primary treasury or escrow rail; MEDIUM for use as a limited operational payment channel only. Legal constraints: a non-resident electronic money institution cannot accept deposits in Canada because the Bank Act reserves the deposit-taking function for Schedule I/II banks and authorized federal credit unions; foreign money-service businesses (MSBs) must either be registered with FINTRAC as a foreign MSB or operate through a FINTRAC-registered Canadian agent; access to the Lynx RTGS and retail payment clearing infrastructures is limited to Payments Canada members; and the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) registration regime will further condition the lawfulness of PSP services. Cross-border EMIs such as Wise Platform or Airwallex may support low-value supplier disbursements but cannot lawfully serve as the escrow clearing hub for large frozen-commodity import settlements or replace a regulated Canadian bank for documentary credit operations
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal statutory mandate requires directors to appear physically in a branch. Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC regulations, identity verification may be completed remotely through (i) a Canadian credit-file check, (ii) dual-process verification of a government-issued photo identity document, or (iii) an independent digital confirmation service. In practice, the six major Schedule I banks require, for a newly incorporated ULC with non-resident beneficial owners, either an in-branch interview with at least one Canadian-resident director or a notarized/legalized KYC package authenticated by a Canadian embassy consular officer or a qualified provincial notary, followed by a mandatory video-verification call. Remote opening is available but is typically routed through the bank's international onboarding desk with enhanced due diligence, and a second-person confirmation is required for the 25%-or-greater UBO

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) structure with layered non-resident shareholdings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incumbency; notarized shareholders' register; UBO declaration table for all natural persons holding 25% or more; trust deed or foundation instrument where the ULC is held through a trust; Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) snapshot; and sworn statutory declaration of control

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or directors domiciled in a high-risk or low-disclosure jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid government-issued passport (notarized true copy); proof of residential address dated within 90 days; tax residency certificate for each UBO/director; reference letter from a bank in their home jurisdiction; source-of-wealth letter with asset accumulation narrative; and commercial rationale statement linking the jurisdiction to the actual frozen-meat supply chain

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC hybrid pass-through tax classification flagged by the bank's tax-risk engine as an aggressive structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canadian legal opinion on the Alberta ULC pass-through election under section 248.1 of the Income Tax Act; Part XIII withholding-tax mapping for deemed dividends; letter of intent confirming no dual-claim or deduction/no-inclusion outcome; and OECD BEPS Action 2 impact assessment

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frozen beef / seafood import supplier invoices inconsistent with industry price benchmarks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SAFE Food for Canadians Act licence; Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) import inspection certificates; executed purchase orders with incoterms; bills of lading and cold-chain warehouse receipts; commercial invoices cross-matched to customs declarations; and reference third-party price verification (e.g., Urner Barry or USDA/DFO commodity indexes)

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name hit against sanctions, terrorist-financing, or politically exposed person (PEP) databases
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed enhanced due diligence file; nationalities and residential history of matched individuals; negative-news analysis; commercial-source explanation for each match; confirmation that no person is a designated individual under the Special Economic Measures Act or Canada's Criminal Code listings; and, where applicable, an OFSI/Global Affairs Canada permit or written determination

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable source of funds for the initial inbound capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the contributing shareholder; 12-month bank statements demonstrating legitimate accumulation; sale and purchase agreements of any asset disposal used to fund the capital; escrow of injected funds pending bank clearance; and a certified subscriber resolution of the ULC approving the share-capital contribution

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from non-resident shareholders is routed through a designated CAD/USD capital escrow account held at a Schedule I OSFI-regulated bank. The injection must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'Equity Contribution / Share Capital Subscription' and reference to the ULC subscriber resolution, using the ISO 20022 remittance field to state 'ISIC 4632 - Wholesale Import of Frozen Meat and Pelagic Fish'. Prior to credit, the bank verifies the Investment Canada Act status: the ULC must file the Notification of Acquisition of Control or Establishment of a New Canadian Business with ISED within 30 days of implementation, and a pre-clearance national-security review may be required regardless of threshold. For sums above US$100,000, the bank will require the full KYC/KYB package and source-of-funds evidence. FINTRAC travel-rule data (originator name, address, and account) must be transmitted on every wire; all EFTs of C$10,000 or more are reportable to FINTRAC within the statutory filing window. Where the shareholder is also the trade supplier, the bank may reclassify the transfer as intercompany trade finance and require a services/merchandise invoice and transfer-pricing documentation
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for frozen beef carcasses and pelagic seafood use a layered clearing-rail structure: (i) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for prepayments, insurance, freight, and post-shipment balance settlements, with the purpose of payment indicating 'Import payment for ISIC 4632 - deep-frozen meat/pelagic fish' and referencing the commercial invoice, bill of lading, and CFIA entry number; (ii) irrevocable confirmed documentary letters of credit issued under UCP600 governing the bulk trade legs, with the Alberta ULC as applicant, a sight or 30-day tenor, and cold-chain inspection certificates as key documents; (iii) standby letters of credit under ISP98 used as performance or warranty instruments; and (iv) documentary collections under URC522 for established repeat-supplier relationships. CAD-denominated obligations clear over Payments Canada's Lynx real-time gross settlement system; USD-denominated obligations clear by the bank's U.S. correspondent network via Fedwire/CHIPS; the is committed to a 'delivered duty paid' clearing point documented by a temperature-recorded warehouse receipt at the designated Canadian cold-chain facility
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright foreign-exchange forwards in CAD/USD and CAD/EUR or other freely tradable counterparty currencies with tenors of up to 24-36 months, documented under the IFEMA master agreement or a bank-dedicated FX line
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps, tom-next swaps, and longer-dated cross-currency interest-rate swaps) used for treasury cash-flow rebalancing, documented under ISDA with a credit-support annex
Vanilla over-the-counter currency options, collars, zero-cost collars, and participating forwards for price-security on seasonal procurement, exercisable through the bank's options desk
Exchange-traded currency options and futures listed on Bourse de Montréal (TMX Group) cleared through the Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation (CDCC)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) strictly limited to exotic non-convertible African, Central Asian, or Latin-American supplier currencies where an onshore deliverable forward market does not exist; the CAD leg remains fully deliverable, making CAD-based NDFs neither customary nor necessary

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 50 (approx. USD 37); continued failure beyond one year permits the Registrar to issue a notice of intention to strike the ULC off the register after 60 days' notice; restoration may be sought within two years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the ULC's taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; repeat failures incur 10% plus 2% per month for up to 20 months; interest is charged on all unpaid amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beef and Veal Import Permit (Tariff Rate Quota Allocation) under the Export and Import Permits Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by October 31 for the following calendar-year allocation (per published GAC allocation notice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Import shipments arriving without a valid permit are refused release by the Canada Border Services Agency; importation without a permit is an offence under the Export and Import Permits Act, subject to fines, imprisonment, and forfeiture of future quota allocations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a private Alberta ULC is not subject to a statutory audit solely by revenue or asset threshold. An auditor must be appointed at each annual general meeting unless all shareholders unanimously resolve to dispense with the audit. Lenders, shareholders, or regulatory authorities may contractually impose an audit, and public or reporting-issuer status will require audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises, or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private ULCs. Cross-border pass-through reporting may mandate IFRS if financial statements are prepared for US or foreign shareholder consolidation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual beneficial-ownership confirmation is filed with Service Alberta. Alberta does not currently maintain a public corporate beneficial-ownership registry. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members, and director changes must be reported via Form 4 Notice of Change of Directors within 15 days. Where the ULC is subject to anti-money-laundering obligations, current UBO records must be maintained for five years after the relationship ends.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 125–360 USD per annum (approximately 150–485 CAD) for registered office and corporate agent services, including annual return preparation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 10,000–22,000 USD per engagement for a private wholesale import ULC, dependent on transaction volume, inventory valuation, and cross-border pass-through complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.00% combined statutory rate (15.00% Federal Part I general rate + 8.00% Alberta general corporate income tax rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Alberta small business deduction: first CAD 500,000 of active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation taxed at 11.00% combined (9.00% Federal + 2.00% Alberta); 100% accelerated CCA on eligible cold-chain equipment and deep-freeze logistics assets; no Alberta capital tax, no provincial payroll tax for wholesale trading; federal investment tax credits for qualified scientific research and experimental development; preferential importer duty treatment under the Canada Border Services Agency duty deferral and bonded warehouse programs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (mandatory EFILE via Canada Revenue Agency certified tax software) combined with Alberta AT1 corporate income tax schedules; Form T106 for non-arm's-length cross-border transactions; Form NR4 for non-resident withholding remittances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual T2/AT1 filing with quarterly or monthly corporate income tax instalments for corporations with taxable income exceeding CAD threshold; NR4 annual return filed by end of February following the calendar year of payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal period end; tax payable balance due within 2 months after fiscal period end for most corporations (3 months for a CCPC eligible for the small business deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income); instalments due at prescribed quarterly dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from wholesale importation and distribution of deep-frozen beef carcasses and pelagic fish, including all cold-chain trading revenue booked through the Alberta permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned ULC, report only Canadian-source gross revenue attributable to the Alberta permanent establishment; non-resident-sourced import commissions and freight revenues should be excluded unless separately allocable to Canadian operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed after deductions for COGS, warehousing, cold-chain logistics, customs duties, interest, and all permitted Alberta and federal commercial deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions only where directly incurred for the PE and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; input allocations must follow the arm's-length principle under section 247 of the Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of corporate income between provinces using gross revenue and salary/wage factors by permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ULCs with only an Alberta PE allocate 100% of taxable income to Alberta; cross-province sales may trigger additional PE allocation filings in other provinces.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 350 / Schedule 1 Federal Part I Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I corporate income tax computed at 15% (or 9% on qualifying small business income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No federal small business deduction is available to a ULC that is not a CCPC; the 15% general rate applies unless treaty provisions or permanent establishment rules alter the base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 91 / Alberta AT1 Corporate Tax Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta corporate tax computed at 8% general rate or 2% small business rate on Alberta-allocated taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be completed for any non-resident ULC carrying on business through an Alberta permanent establishment; Alberta income tax is imposed on the taxable income allocated to Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T106 Information Return for Transactions with Non-Residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of each non-arm's-length transaction with a related non-resident corporation, including import purchase prices, royalties, interest, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for controlled cross-border transactions; must be filed within 6 months of the taxation year-end and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual record of non-resident withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, and management fees paid to shareholders or related parties outside Canada.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The ULC must withhold 25% statutory Part XIII tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders unless treaty relief has been validated via Form NR301 or an approved withholding certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under section 162(1) of the Income Tax Act: 5.00% of the unpaid balance plus 1.00% per full month for up to 12 months; arrears interest at the prescribed daily rate; section 163(2) civil penalty of 50% for false statements or omissions made knowingly or in circumstances amounting to gross negligence; failure to file T106 triggers fixed monthly penalties under section 162(7.1) up to CAD 24,000; Alberta Education Property Tax and Corporate Tax penalties mirror federal structure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25.00% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident ULC to non-resident shareholders; no exemption at source unless treaty relief is granted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident US shareholder must obtain a valid US IRS Form 6166 certificate of residency, complete and submit Form NR301 (Declaration of Entitlement to Treaty Benefits), and provide this to the Canadian payer before or at the time of payment; the ULC is entitled to reduce withholding to 5.00% where the US corporate shareholder owns at least 10% of the voting stock of the ULC, or 15.00% in other cases; Canada-US Fifth Protocol (2023) limitation-on-benefits provisions require substantive commercial activity and base-erosion compliance, with mandatory self-certification by corporate claimants.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate 25.00% for royalties and interest; under the Canada-US treaty, interest generally reduced to 15.00% effective from 2024 (previously 10.00% in certain arm's-length cases); royalties reduced to 0.00% for patents, copyrights, know-how, and computer software and 10.00% for trademarks, films, and similar industrial property; treaty relief requires Form NR301 and TRC; Canada does not impose Part XIII withholding on most arm's-length interest paid to foreign financial institutions if the recipient deals at arm's length and the payer is wholly taxable in Canada.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for controlled transactions with any non-resident where the aggregate gross value of controlled transactions exceeds CAD 5,000,000 in a taxation year; Master File and Local File required for Canadian members of MNE groups with consolidated group revenue equal to or exceeding CAD 800,000,000; Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) filed at the same revenue threshold; penalty trigger where a transfer pricing adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5,000,000 or 10.00% of gross revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No named Economic Substance Regulation exists in Canadian federal or Alberta law, but economic substance is statutorily enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 245 of the Income Tax Act), which disallows avoidance transactions lacking a bona fide business purpose, and through the Canada-US treaty Limitation-on-Benefits article requiring substantive business activity, public-listing status, or 90% qualified-ownership plus a 50% base-erosion test; the ULC remains a taxable Canadian corporation that cannot accept hybrid-status deductions in Canada; treaty benefits are denied where the entity is a conduit, shell, or lacks real economic capacity, premises, personnel, and cold-chain trading substance in Alberta.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Filing (Section 239 Income Tax Act)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of frozen meat and seafood import revenues, falsification of shipping documents to understate taxable income, deliberate under-reporting of beef carcass and pelagic fish contract values, or systematic misclassification of capital gains as non-taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On summary conviction, a fine of not less than 50.00% and not more than 200.00% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 2 years; on indictment, the same fine plus imprisonment up to 5 years; civil gross-negligence penalty under section 163(2) of 50.00% of the understated tax; revocation of business licences and securities of the frozen-food import entry under the Customs Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable under section 227.1 for unremitted Part XIII withholding tax and unpaid corporate tax where due diligence is not exercisable; CRA may issue a section 226 departure-restriction notice requiring security before the director leaves Canada; criminal conviction triggers travel restrictions, enforcement of restitution orders, and seizure of personal and corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Sham Import Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-pricing related-party purchases of frozen beef and seafood to shift profits to low-tax foreign affiliates, using documentary-only transactions with shell warehouses, or creating circular cold-chain logistics fees without real economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10.00% transfer pricing penalty on the net adjustment under section 247(3) where the adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5,000,000 or 10.00% of gross revenue; reassessment of arm's-length profits; interest accrual from the original filing deadline; secondary T106 late-filing penalties up to CAD 24,000 per form; Customs valuation penalties for fraudulent invoices under the Customs Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unremitted Part XIII amounts and penalties where they authorized or acquiesced in the fraudulent invoicing; criminal charges can attach to signing officers; CRA enforcement includes garnishment, liens, and section 226 departure interdiction for tax debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of a non-resident-owned ULC without employees, warehouse capacity, board control, or real decision-making functions in Alberta; stripping profits through excessive dividends, royalties, or interest to a US parent solely to claim lower convention rates; failure to maintain contemporaneous documentation for the 5.00% treaty dividend rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR denial of all tax benefits, including dividend withholding relief and losses; 15.00% GAAR penalty where the CRA applies the avoidance-transaction penalty provisions of the Income Tax Act; denial of Canada-US treaty benefits under the Limitation-on-Benefits Article, creating exposure to the full 25.00% Part XIII withholding rate; Alberta corporate registry dissolution and loss of ULC capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unremitted withholding tax and for corporate tax where funds have been distributed before CRA assessment; civil restitution orders in favour of the Crown; travel bans are available in respect of unpaid assessments where the individual is scheduled to depart Canada; foreign criminal assistance mechanisms facilitate extradition in aggravated fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring cash transactions above CAD 10,000, accepting concentrated high-risk wire transfers from shell-company buyers without beneficial-ownership verification, falsified bills of lading for frozen meat trans-shipments, or failure to register and maintain a compliance regime despite qualifying as a money services business or importer-dealer subject to FINTRAC obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for corporate violators and CAD 100,000 for individuals; suspension of import licences; seizure of undeclared monetary instruments under the Customs Act; criminal money-laundering penalties up to CAD 2,000,000 or imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment; freezing orders and forfeiture of corruptly acquired cold-chain assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers personally subject to regulatory enforcement for failure to report suspicious transactions; personal liability for large-cash-transaction penalties where the director exercised control; conviction triggers imprisonment, post-conviction travel restrictions, disgorgement of profits, and permanent disqualification from federally regulated insured activities.
